cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Test the Impossible Claim
cards.instruction: Get someone else to take the first practical step that could prove the bizarre claim true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This tap gives you whatever you ask for. Ask for tea while I hold a cup; I'll supervise the test.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're not using my good china.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A saucepan will do. We're testing the tap, not the crockery. I'll hold it; you make the request.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask, but I'm not tasting anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then request a biscuit. We need a result we can identify by sight. Please don't put your tongue into the experiment.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 distinguishes the experimental object from the vessel and A5 visual identification from taste, supervising B's first request to the impossible tap.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 china condition changes A3 vessel; B4 taste boundary changes A5 requested output.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects possessions and B4 bodily safety, giving A legitimate constraints to accommodate.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 tasting refusal to devise a visible biscuit test while leaving the first request with B.

specificity.evidence: A1 wish-granting tap and cup make the experiment explicit; A3 saucepan is a direct substitute.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 tongue remark is a pointed endorsement of B4 refusal, though its imperative could sound unfairly corrective.
